title: 门店体验要改进，怎样提出一个可试行的方案？
topic: 根据顾客反馈提出门店体验试点

source.title: Designing Interactive Stores that ‘Wow’
source.type: 沃尔玛官方零售体验设计案例
source.context: 沃尔玛 沃尔玛官方零售体验设计案例。
paragraphs: For millions of customers, our stores and associates are the reason they love Walmart. They are the greatest assets for our brand. We’re always listening to our customers’ and associates’ feedback to help inspire, evolve and refresh the store experience.

In today’s omnichannel world, customers still want to experience – touch, feel and try – items. So, we’re now aiming to make customers feel wowed and proud when they shop with us. We’re using powerful design elements to show off amazing products that wow our customers, and when they see the value, they are proud of their choice and purchase.

Last year, we announced the first phase of our store redesign that was focused on navigation and wayfinding. The feedback was overwhelmingly positive, and we now have close to 1,000 stores renovated with this new design to help customers save time in finding what they need.

In this next phase of our redesign, we’re amplifying the physical, human and digital design elements in our stores to inspire customers and elevate the experience. Physical elements include lighting, space enhancements, dynamic displays and more. Our visual merchandising experts have highlighted exciting brands and created engaging experiences that bring to life the human element. Finally, QR codes and digital screens create opportunities for digital exploration. But making the store more engaging isn’t enough. We have to do all of this in a way that is unique to Walmart.

Digital touchpoints: Using our stores as an initial display of the great variety of products and brands, we can communicate to customers the vast range of products and services Walmart offers online through the strategic use of QR codes and digital screens. For example, in our Pets area, a customer may scan the QR code to find additional dog bed options, learn about Walmart’s pet insurance service options or have a 20-pound bag of kibble delivered to their door.

We’ll continue to test, learn, and make changes based on what our customers tell us. As we do that, we’ll quickly adjust and deliver an even better, more engaging experience in 2022 and beyond. After all, when customers choose to shop in-store with us, we want them to feel wowed and inspired – and that their time was well spent.
translations: 对数百万顾客来说，沃尔玛门店和员工正是他们喜爱沃尔玛的原因，也是品牌最重要的资产。我们一直听取顾客和员工的反馈，以此启发、发展和更新门店体验。
在全渠道零售时代，顾客仍希望亲自体验商品——触摸、感受和试用。因此，我们希望顾客在店购物时感到惊喜，也为自己的选择感到自豪。我们通过有感染力的设计展示优质商品；当顾客看到商品的价值时，也会为自己的选择和购买感到自豪。
去年，我们宣布门店改造的第一阶段，重点是导航和寻路指引。顾客反馈非常积极，目前近 1,000 家门店已完成改造，帮助顾客更快找到需要的商品。
在改造的下一阶段，我们会加强门店的实体、人员和数字设计元素，以吸引顾客、提升体验。实体设计包括灯光、空间优化和动态陈列等；视觉陈列团队会突出特色品牌，打造有参与感的体验。二维码和数字屏幕则提供线上探索的入口。不过，门店有趣还不够，所有设计还必须体现沃尔玛自身的特点。
门店可以先展示丰富的商品和品牌，再通过二维码和数字屏幕向顾客介绍沃尔玛线上提供的商品与服务。例如，在宠物用品区，顾客可以扫描二维码查看更多狗床款式、了解宠物保险，或把一袋 20 磅重的狗粮送到家。
我们会继续测试、学习并根据顾客反馈进行调整，快速改进体验，并在 2022 年及以后打造更好、更吸引人的购物体验。顾客选择到店购物时，我们希望他们感到惊喜、受到启发，也觉得这趟时间值得。
fullTextParagraphs: By Alvis Washington, Vice President, Marketing Store Design, Innovation and Experience

For millions of customers, our stores and associates are the reason they love Walmart. They are the greatest assets for our brand. We’re always listening to our customers’ and associates’ feedback to help inspire, evolve and refresh the store experience.

Today, we’re unveiling a new, signature experience in our incubator location, Store 4108 in Springdale, Arkansas, that we call “Time Well Spent.” It focuses on making Walmart a destination where customers want to spend their time.

In today’s omnichannel world, customers still want to experience – touch, feel and try – items. So, we’re now aiming to make customers feel wowed and proud when they shop with us. We’re using powerful design elements to show off amazing products that wow our customers, and when they see the value, they are proud of their choice and purchase.

Last year, we announced the first phase of our store redesign that was focused on navigation and wayfinding. The feedback was overwhelmingly positive, and we now have close to 1,000 stores renovated with this new design to help customers save time in finding what they need.

In this next phase of our redesign, we’re amplifying the physical, human and digital design elements in our stores to inspire customers and elevate the experience. Physical elements include lighting, space enhancements, dynamic displays and more. Our visual merchandising experts have highlighted exciting brands and created engaging experiences that bring to life the human element. Finally, QR codes and digital screens create opportunities for digital exploration. But making the store more engaging isn’t enough. We have to do all of this in a way that is unique to Walmart.
Here are our guiding design principles for the redesign:

Activated corners: Exciting displays at the corners of certain departments pull customers in and help them touch, feel and become a part of the space, allowing them to discover all that we have to offer. Home may feature a living room or bedroom set up where the customer can squeeze a throw pillow or feel the coziness of a blanket, then find those items onsite to purchase and take home, or order them online.

Home may feature a living room or bedroom set up where the customer can squeeze a throw pillow or feel the coziness of a blanket, then find those items onsite to purchase and take home, or order them online.

Elevated brand shops: Taking a “store within a store experience” to the next level. Apparel will highlight owned and national brands. Great prices are a given, but we’ll celebrate quality and style, in style.New parents will not want for inspiration when they visit the Baby department. They will be greeted by elevated displays showcasing all the items needed to create a dream nursery as well as strollers and car seats that are brought out of the box to allow for test drives.Beauty will also showcase exciting shops where new and trending items are given a home, and men’s grooming tools can be seen and experienced.
Apparel will highlight owned and national brands. Great prices are a given, but we’ll celebrate quality and style, in style.

New parents will not want for inspiration when they visit the Baby department. They will be greeted by elevated displays showcasing all the items needed to create a dream nursery as well as strollers and car seats that are brought out of the box to allow for test drives.
Beauty will also showcase exciting shops where new and trending items are given a home, and men’s grooming tools can be seen and experienced.

More space to discover: In these new reimagined spaces, we have purposefully created more space for our customers to explore and discover the breadth and depth of what our stores have to offer, and we’ve optimized assortment to elevate storytelling that draws customers in.

Digital touchpoints: Using our stores as an initial display of the great variety of products and brands, we can communicate to customers the vast range of products and services Walmart offers online through the strategic use of QR codes and digital screens. For example, in our Pets area, a customer may scan the QR code to find additional dog bed options, learn about Walmart’s pet insurance service options or have a 20-pound bag of kibble delivered to their door.
Early results show that customers are wowed by the redesign. I love hearing customers say this is their favorite Walmart store, and it makes me proud to be a part of the team leading this work.

We’ll continue to test, learn, and make changes based on what our customers tell us. As we do that, we’ll quickly adjust and deliver an even better, more engaging experience in 2022 and beyond. After all, when customers choose to shop in-store with us, we want them to feel wowed and inspired – and that their time was well spent.

scenario.title: 模拟门店体验试点：帮助顾客比较商品
english: Customers want to try products in person and compare more options before buying.
Your team could test a hands-on display with a QR code in one department.
You need to explain the customer benefit and agree on how to review the pilot.
chinese: 顾客想在购买前亲自体验商品，并比较更多选择。
团队可以在一个部门试行体验式陈列和二维码。
你需要说明顾客能得到什么，并商定如何复盘试点。

firstAttempt.prompt: 请用英语提出一项门店体验试点，说明顾客能得到什么，以及你们会用什么数据和反馈来复盘。
firstAttempt.sample: Customers want to try products in person and compare more options. Could we test a hands-on display with a QR code in one department? It would let shoppers try the product and see the full range online. We’ll track QR scans and purchases in the pilot stores, then review customer feedback after four weeks.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先说顾客需求，再提出小范围测试，并用顾客行为和反馈判断是否有效。

taskPhrases.collocation: test a new experience in one department
taskPhrases.example: Could we test a hands-on display in one department?
taskPhrases.translation: 我们能否在一个部门试行体验式陈列？

taskPhrases.example: It would let shoppers try the product and compare more options.
taskPhrases.translation: 这样顾客就能试用商品并比较更多选择。

taskPhrases.example: We’ll track QR scans and purchases, then review feedback after four weeks.
taskPhrases.translation: 我们会跟踪二维码扫描和购买情况，并在四周后复盘顾客反馈。

words.example: Clear wayfinding helps shoppers find products faster.
words.translation: 清楚的路线指引能帮助顾客更快找到商品。
words.note: 常用于门店、园区和网站导航。

words.example: A QR code can be a useful digital touchpoint in store.
words.translation: 二维码可以成为门店里的一个数字互动入口。
words.note: 指顾客与品牌或服务互动的具体入口。

words.example: The company renovated several stores to improve navigation.
words.translation: 公司改造了几家门店，以改善顾客导航体验。
words.note: 常用于改造门店、办公室或建筑。

structure.original: We’ll continue to test, learn, and make changes based on what our customers tell us.
analysis: test, learn, and make changes 按顺序说明试点、收集信息、再调整。
based on what…tell us 说明改动依据来自顾客反馈。
structure.transfer: We’ll test the new pickup process, review customer comments, and make changes based on what we learn.

rewrite.bad: Let’s make the store more exciting with more screens.
rewrite.good: Customers want to try products in person and compare more options. Could we test a hands-on display with a QR code in one department? We’ll track how shoppers use it and review their feedback after four weeks.
rewrite.translation: 顾客想亲自体验商品并比较更多选择。我们能否在一个部门试行体验式陈列和二维码？我们会跟踪顾客的使用情况，并在四周后复盘反馈。
rewrite.pattern: Customers want [need]. Could we test [change] in [scope]? We’ll track [behavior] and review [feedback] after [period].

cloze.why: test a change 表示试行一项改动。

cloze.prompt: It would let customers ______ the product in person.
cloze.why: try a product 表示亲自试用商品。

cloze.prompt: We’ll track QR scans and ______ after four weeks.
cloze.why: purchase data 可用于观察顾客是否采取了下一步行动。

dictation.text: Customers still want to touch, feel, and try items.

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否在一个部门试行体验式陈列？
translationPractice.answer: Could we test a hands-on display in one department?

translationPractice.answer: It would let shoppers try the product and compare more options.
translationPractice.why: 说明顾客能获得的实际好处。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们会跟踪二维码扫描和购买情况，并在四周后复盘顾客反馈。
translationPractice.answer: We’ll track QR scans and purchases, then review feedback after four weeks.

choice.prompt: 门店体验试点一个月后，哪组信息最适合决定是否扩大？
options: The new display looks more modern.
Customers used the display, scanned the QR code, and several asked for more product options. Sales and feedback improved in the pilot department.
The team spent a lot of time preparing the display.
choice.why: 结合顾客使用行为、购买情况和反馈判断实际效果。

output.prompt: 你准备在一家门店测试新的自助取货指引。请说明顾客遇到的问题、试点改动，以及要跟踪的指标。
output.sample: Customers often wait in the wrong area for online orders. Could we test clearer pickup signs and a QR code at one store? We’ll track the time customers spend finding the pickup point and review staff feedback after two weeks.
check: 描述顾客遇到的具体问题
说明要跟踪的顾客指标和复盘时间
